scenario: Scenario 2: A stale session-open overwrites the owner of a live connection
notes: MC-2 (REPRODUCED) reached the target. The mechanism combines FAULT and INTERLEAVING. The FAULT is a 2-3 s delay on the follower-to-leader link, longer than the client connectTimeout but shorter than syncLimit*tickTime, so no peer fails. The INTERLEAVING is a client that abandons the follower handshake and reopens at the leader before the delayed REVALIDATE is processed. The chain of events: the client reopens its session at follower F, and F writes a REVALIDATE that is held on the F->L link. The client's connect times out, so it reopens at leader L, which sets owner = ServerCnxn.me. The stale REVALIDATE then reaches L, where LearnerHandler runs setOwner(id, this) without checking that the handshake is still current. From then on, every op on the client's live connection to L fails checkSession, and the guard session.owner != owner throws SessionMovedException at SessionTrackerImpl.java:246. Reproduction: a variant of TestAdhocWorkloadK1 on unmodified base-commit sources triggered it in 4 of 4 runs (one Ant run plus three direct runs with a read-only JDI observer that captured the frame), and 12 of 12 ops failed. The pinned tree lacks the ZOOKEEPER-710 mitigation. MC-1 (MASKED) also reaches L246 with no fault: a follower-forwarded sync carries a null owner, so the check fails on every follower sync. That exception is swallowed: Prep only logs it, ProposalRequestProcessor/Leader.processSync ignore it, and the follower answers the sync locally, so the client gets OK. CR-1 and CR-3 were judged FALSE POSITIVE. The convergence config MC.cfg (no faults; 1573 distinct states, depth 36) found no violation, and MC_sanity_reach.cfg confirmed TargetCheck is reachable. Bounds per bug-report.md: 2 followers and at most 2-3 client ops and reopens. Both hunts stopped at their first violation.
